claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex.

Now, could you please tell me if you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. Now, could you tell me about your living situation with Alex? Does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a couple more questions to confirm eligibility:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question: Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation, or has he been for an extended period recently?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - he's been in hospital for quite a while now, a few months actually. He's been getting treatment there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been in hospital. I hope his treatment is going well.

Since Alex has been in hospital for a few months, I need to ask a couple of follow-up questions as this can affect Child Benefit eligibility:

Has Alex been in hospital continuously for more than 12 weeks?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been longer than that - about 15 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, there are some exceptions that may still allow you to receive Child Benefit.

Could you tell me if you regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital? This could include things like buying him clothes, toys, food treats, or other items for his comfort and care.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, unfortunately I haven't been able to afford to spend money on his needs while he's in there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being open about that. I understand that hospital stays can be financially challenging.

Just to make sure I have all the relevant information: Is Alex in a hospital in the UK, or is he abroad for treatment?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's in a hospital here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 8 years old and is your son
- You live in the UK
- Alex normally lives with you
- He has been in a UK hospital for approximately 15 weeks (which is more than 12 weeks)
- You are not regularly spending money on him while he's in hospital
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

Let me now provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

- Normally, you would qualify for Child Benefit as Alex is under 16, lives with you, and you're in the UK.
- However, when a child has been in hospital for **more than 12 weeks**, Child Benefit eligibility is usually affected.
- There is an exception that allows you to continue receiving Child Benefit if you **regularly spend money** on your child while they're in hospital (for example, on clothes, treats, or other items for their comfort).
- Since you've mentioned you haven't been able to afford to spend money on Alex's needs while he's in hospital, this exception does not currently apply.

**What you can do:**

- If your circumstances change and you begin regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital, you may become eligible again. I would recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office to discuss your situation.
- Once Alex leaves hospital and returns home, you should be able to claim Child Benefit again. You would need to make a new claim at that point.

I'm truly sorry this isn't better news, and I hope Alex recovers well and is home with you soon.

The claimant has confirmed they have not been able to afford to spend money on Alex's needs while he's in hospital. Since the 12-week limit has been exceeded and the exception for regularly spending money on the child does not apply, the claimant is not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
